transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-10-16
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Maya Shah (Redwood SE), Ethan Lowe (Redwood CSM); Liam Torres (CTO), Priya Desai (Lead ML), Samir Rao (Platform)

Auto-generated summary (brief):
- Quick qualification of Seedling's plan to move from prototype to PLG self-serve; emphasis on time-to-first-token and cost controls.
- Discussed hosted API for quick onboarding vs Dedicated/Private for compliance/residency.
- Seedling asked about free credits, SSO, KMS, and pilot benchmarking.
- Next: Redwood to provision credits, send security pack, schedule bench run.

Topics detected: onboarding credits, hosted vs private, latency tradeoffs, security and VPC, pilot success criteria, bench runs

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um today's just a quick handoff / discovery for the credits and to make sure we set expectations on time-to-first-token. I think we have 45 minutes, is that right?
[00:12] Liam Torres: Yep that's perfect. Thanks Jordan. We, sort of off the bat, want the easiest way to get engineers to call the API and validate it's fast enough for product.
[00:20] Maya Shah: Great. Quick intro from my side, I'm Maya, I focus on performance and private deployments. We'll talk through hosted, then the Dedicated/reserved and VPC options if you'd like.
[00:29] Priya Desai: Awesome. Our main constraints — we want sub-200ms P95 for short prompts (one-shot completion) and cost under $0.0008 per token equivalent in production if possible. For prototype, it's looser.
[00:42] Samir Rao: And on infra side we need SSO, audit logs, and ability to bring our own KMS eventually. Also data residency for EU users down the road.
[00:52] Jordan Kim: Cool. So two threads: immediate PLG path (credits, quickstart, time-to-first-token) and then the enterprise path (Dedicated / Private) as you scale. Is that fair?
[01:01] Liam Torres: Yes, exactly. We want to be able to hand devs a token today and measure latency in a few hours.
[01:08] Maya Shah: The hosted Redwood API is built for that: self-serve API keys, streaming responses, and an onboarding flow. We'll give you a credits bundle — that lets you spin up quick tests without billing.
[01:17] Priya Desai: Two questions: how long does a token activate and is there rate-limiting on free credits?
[01:23] Jordan Kim: Tokens issue immediately. Free credits are rate-limited to prevent abuse, we can increase limits for pilot bench runs if needed — that's something we'll coordinate.
[01:32] [00:32] Priya Desai: Sorry, did you say there is per-account rate-limiting or per-key?
[01:36] Maya Shah: Per-key default; for bench runs we usually lift them or provision a dedicated credit bucket so you can saturate the route for a short window.
[01:45] Samir Rao: For the bench we'd want to test both batching behaviors and KV cache hit rates — is there a way to see token-level breakdowns?
[01:53] Jordan Kim: Yes, Redwood Console shows token-level cost and latency breakdowns per model and route. We'll share a short video, but Maya can also walk through how to interpret the breakdowns.
[02:05] Maya Shah: One thing to note, batching helps but increases tail latency when you push throughput. For your target P95, we can recommend model and batching configs.
[02:14] Liam Torres: Ok — if we started with hosted, what's the expected path and timeline to Dedicated or Private if we need it?
[02:21] Jordan Kim: Typical pattern: hosted for PLG and early product tests (minutes to first call), Dedicated reserved capacity when you need predictable throughput and an SLA (weeks to provision), Private (VPC or on-prem) for regulated or full isolation (30–60 days depending on region and HSM/KMS needs).
[02:36] Priya Desai: For Private, how do you handle KMS? We don't want keys leaving our control.
[02:41] Maya Shah: We integrate with customer KMS — you can bring a cloud KMS or an HSM. The private control plane keeps metadata but you maintain keys. There's an on-prem packaging option for air-gapped environments as well, though that's heavier.
[02:55] Samir Rao: Any special network requirements for VPC peering? Our infra team is particular about routes and egress.
[03:02] Jordan Kim: We typically do VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on cloud. We'll send the network runbook with IP ranges and egress policies.
[03:10] [03:10] Priya Desai: Ok thanks. Back to credits, can we tie credits to a team and limit them so the marketing folks don't blow the budget?
[03:18] Ethan Lowe: Yes— we have token-level quotas and can scope credits to org units. For PLG you'll usually give dev teams a small per-dev allocation and then a shared pilot pool for benchmark runs.
[03:28] Liam Torres: Good. We also want to validate output quality — are there quick tools to run prompt sets and flag regressions?
[03:34] Maya Shah: Redwood Optimize includes basic eval tooling and you can upload prompt/response pairs to monitor drift or quality regressions. For an initial pilot we normally run a short eval harness.
[03:44] Priya Desai: That sounds useful. For the benchmark next week — what do you need from us?
[03:49] Jordan Kim: Ideally a small prompt set (20–50 prompts) that represent your production distribution, desired concurrency, and any example of worst-case long-context prompts. Also your target latency and acceptable quality thresholds.
[03:59] Priya Desai: We can assemble that by Friday.
[04:02] [04:02] Liam Torres: I wanted to talk about pricing friction: if we go hosted but later move to Dedicated, do credits or usage apply to committed consumption?
[04:10] Jordan Kim: Credits are for self-serve usage only and don't map to reserved capacity; however, our sales/finance team will give transition credits or commit discounts as you scale — we can model that once we know volumes.
[04:21] Samir Rao: Competitor question: how does Redwood differ from Anthropic or straight-up self-hosting?
[04:26] Maya Shah: Anthropic is similar on models/APIs; the key Redwood differentiator is the production runtime and routing — unified interface across hosted/dedicated/private and tooling for cost/perf tradeoffs like KV cache, batching profiles, and automated fallbacks. Self-hosting gives control but you'll invest heavily in ops for the same runtime features.
[04:45] Priya Desai: Any common gotchas people hit when they start?
[04:48] Maya Shah: Two big ones: not configuring batching/timeout profiles so tail latency spikes; and not instrumenting token-level cost which causes surprise bills. We'll help set sane defaults.
[04:58] Liam Torres: For SSO, we use Okta — what's the flow?
[05:02] Jordan Kim: SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning is supported; it takes a day or two for mapping groups and roles once we have your IdP metadata.
[05:11] Priya Desai: What about audit logs retention? We need 365 days for compliance.
[05:16] Ethan Lowe: We can configure extended retention as an add-on for enterprise plans; hosted default is shorter, but Dedicated/Private provide richer log control. We'll include retention options in the pack.
[05:27] [05:27] Samir Rao: Small dev question: do you support the standard OpenAI-style endpoints (like chat completions) or is it a different shape?
[05:33] Jordan Kim: We support a familiar REST/SDK interface including chat and generate endpoints; we also have streaming and tool-calling primitives. Some parameter names vary but we have client SDKs in JS/Python.
[05:45] Priya Desai: Perfect. Can we mention the SLA numbers for Dedicated?
[05:49] Maya Shah: Dedicated SLA is typically 99.9% uptime for the inference plane and latency SLOs that we agree on per-deployment. We'll add exact numbers in the proposal.
[05:59] Liam Torres: Great. For the bench, what level of throughput can you emulate on hosted?
[06:05] Maya Shah: We can provision higher rate limits for short windows or give you a test key that bypasses soft limits. For sustained high throughput we recommend Dedicated.
[06:14] Priya Desai: Ok. Quick question on observability: do we get per-route traces or just aggregated metrics?
[06:20] Maya Shah: Both. The Console shows aggregated costs and latency, and we support tracing hooks and per-token logs for debugging. Those per-token logs can be restricted for PII concerns.
[06:31] Jordan Kim: Alright, small recap and next steps: we'll provision credits, send the security + network runbook, and set up a 1-hour bench next Tue to run your prompt set. Anything else?
[06:42] Liam Torres: Can you also include a sample cURL/SDK snippet for the exact headers and token exchange? That helps our devs quicker.
[06:48] Jordan Kim: Absolutely, we'll put that in the onboarding email.
[06:51] Priya Desai: One last thing — how do you handle model rollbacks if a new version degrades quality?
[06:56] Maya Shah: We support pinned model versions per route and rollout policies (canary/A-B) with automatic fallback to previous pinned version. You can tie eval tests to rollout gates in Redwood Console.
[07:06] Samir Rao: Awesome. That covers it for me.
[07:08] Jordan Kim: Great thanks everyone. We'll follow up today with the credits and docs.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription quality: medium — occasional overlapping talk, some product names may be slightly mis-typed (e.g., K V cache sometimes appears as KV cash). Several timestamps are approximate because of automated markers.
